en: The *Śivatāṇḍavastotra* is considered to have been composed by the great scholar and supreme devotee of Śiva, Rāvaṇa, the lord of Laṅkā. May Śiva grant us auspiciousness—he who, on a ground purified by the flowing streams of water trickling from his matted locks, having draped around his neck a lofty garland of serpents, performed a fierce *tāṇḍava* dance accompanied by the deep, resonant sound of his *ḍamaru* drum: *ḍama-ḍḍama-ḍḍama-ḍḍaman*. (1)

My delight is at every moment in Him who bears the crescent moon as His crest-jewel; upon whose head shines a mass of matted locks like a churning cauldron from which flows the stream of Nīla, and where the creeper-like waves toss about; and upon whose forehead-plate the fire blazes with a "dhag-dhag-dhag" roar.

May that object which delights the mind find its place somewhere in this vast expanse—she who is the daughter of the king of mountains, whose playful charm makes the series of directions beautiful and radiant, whose heart overflows with joy, and who has warded off insurmountable calamities with a stream of compassionate glances. 3.

In the Lord of Beings, who brings wonder and delight to the mind, the faces of the women of the quarters are smeared with saffron paste from the mass of radiance of the flickering crest-jewels of the tawny serpents in his matted locks;
he is radiant with the upper garment of the shimmering skin of a rut-maddened elephant.
May he whose footstool is greyed by the showers of pollen from the flowers crowning the crests of all the gods, beginning with the thousand-eyed Indra;
who wears a mass of matted locks bound with a garland of the king of serpents; and who has the friend of the cakora bird as his crest-ornament—may he long grant us prosperity. (5)

May the head of the Great Skull-Bearer—whose matted locks are crowned with a crescent moon shining like nectar, whose forehead is marked by the five arrows of the God of Love appearing as sparks from the blazing fire of the third eye, and who is bowed to by the Lord of the Nīlins—be for our supreme prosperity. 6.
My devotion is fixed on the Three-Eyed Lord, whose forehead-plate bears a fire that crackles and blazes intensely, who holds the fierce five-arrowed god as his bow,
and who is the sole master artisan in crafting the decorative leaf-designs upon the breasts of the Mountain King’s daughter.
May the Lord who bears the burden of the world—He whose neck is firmly held up as the darkness of the night was dispelled by the shimmering moon obstructed by a fresh circle of clouds;
He who wears the mountain from which flow the streams of the celestial Ganges; and who is as beautiful as the repository of all arts—bestow prosperity upon us.
I worship Him who mocks the dark luster of a cluster of full-blown blue lotuses, whose neck possesses a mass of splendor like that of a serpent,

who is the destroyer of Smara, the destroyer of the cities [of the demons], the destroyer of worldly existence, the destroyer of the sacrifice [of Dakṣa], the destroyer of the elephant [Gaja], the destroyer of Andhaka, and the destroyer of Death himself.

I worship Him who is the destroyer of Smara, the destroyer of Tripura, the destroyer of Bhava, the destroyer of Makha, the destroyer of Gaja, the destroyer of Andhaka, and the destroyer of Tamas— the one who is the flow of the sweetness of the essence of the cluster of blossoms of all auspiciousness that is never small.

May Śiva’s fierce *tāṇḍava* dance bring victory— a dance set in motion by the succession of lofty, auspicious sounds of mṛdaṅga drums resounding "dhimiddhimiddhimi," while his forehead-fire blazes with a terrifying "dhagaddhaga" as it flashes forth from the serpent coiled upon his brow, which whirls with vast, cloud-like grace.

When shall I worship Sadāśiva, making my mind regard as equal a variegated couch and a slab of stone, a necklace of serpent-pearls and a gem and a clod of earth, a friend and an enemy faction, and the lotus-eyed Lord and the sovereign of the world? 12.

When, dwelling in the hollow of a bower by the Nilimpa waterfall, forever freed from evil thoughts, constantly bearing my joined palms upon my head, with restless eyes cast aside and the forehead-mark applied to my brow, shall I, chanting the mantra "Śiva," finally become happy? (13)

May that mass of radiance born from his limbs, enchanting with the intense sweetness dripping from the intermingling of the jasmine flowers atop the crests of the multitude of Nāga lords of the Nīlimpa city, bestow upon us delightful joy of mind day and night as it takes refuge in the Supreme Abode. 14.

May that which spreads the auspicious radiance of the fierce submarine fire, which desires the eight great supernatural powers, whose discourse is invoked by the people, whose left eye is ever-free, whose sound is like the resonance at the time of a wedding, and which is adorned with the mantra "Śiva"—may it arise for the conquest of the world. 15.
Indeed, a person who constantly recites, remembers, and speaks this supreme hymn of ever-liberated liberation attains perpetual purity.

He quickly gains true devotion for Hari and his Guru, and never again falls into a state of delusion; for the contemplation of the Great Benefactor (Śiva) is the ultimate good for embodied beings. 16.
Regarding the declaration of the fruit:

Śambhu always bestows upon that person a steady and gracious fortune, accompanied by chariots, lordly elephants, and horses, who at the conclusion of the worship recites during the evening twilight this hymn sung by the Ten-faced One (Rāvaṇa), which is devoted to the adoration of Śambhu. (17)
Thus ends the hymn to Śiva’s Tāṇḍava dance composed by Rāvaṇa.
